thread.title: Silicon Valley stock index drops as Apple, Facebook, Alphabet shares fall

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Silicon Valley stock index drops as Apple, Facebook, Alphabet shares fall

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high technology index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley   2:33pm PST Shares of the world's most valuable company, Apple , fell 1.59 percent on Wednesday, dragging down an index of Silicon Valley's biggest stocks and capping a volatile day of trading on Wall Street. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index , an index of 13 of the biggest technology stocks in the region, dipped 0.99 percent on Wednesday, with the decline led by Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). Shares in the Cupertino-based company fell after Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi predicted lower iPhone sales . He projects, based on conversations with people in Apple's supply chain, that sales of the devices may decline about 33 percent between the December 2017 and March 2018 quarters. Several of the other tech giants also slumped. Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) fell 1.48 percent on Wednesday while Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) dipped 0.49 percent. Among all Silicon Valley-based stocks, solar manufacturer SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR) experienced the biggest decline. Shares of the San Jose-based company dropped 4.78 percent, after falling more than 6 percent on Tuesday, as its CEO asked for an exemption to a new 30 percent tariff on solar cell imports in exchange for a new "pilot" factory in San Jose . Other Silicon Valley stocks that fell: • Shares of Synaptics (NASDAQ: SYNA) declined 3.63 percent. • Cypress Semiconductor Corp. (NASDAQ: CY) dropped 3.49 percent. • Maxim Integrated Products (NASDAQ: MXIM) slipped 2.84 percent. • VeriFone Systems (NYSE: PAY) closed down 2.8 percent. Top-performing Silicon Valley stocks on Wednesday: • Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) surged for a third day straight, closing up 4.4 percent. The Los Gatos-based company reported expectation-busting quarterly results on Monday. • Varian Medical Systems (NYSE: VAR) shares gained 2.02 percent. Ranked by Local employee headcount Rank
